name: run-error-then-new-run-continues
description: RUN_ERROR does not end the stream: a RUN_STARTED after it begins a new run in the same stream, and everything the second run produces is applied and delivered
kill: drop the RUN_ERROR arm from resetRunState's caller in verifyEvents so a RUN_STARTED after a RUN_ERROR is rejected as nested, or make the reducer's RUN_ERROR case end the stream (a `throwError` after `emitUpdates()`) — either way the second run's message never arrives and `messages`, `eventTypes` and `outcome` fail together

dotnet.intentional: The .NET converter forbids any event after RUN_ERROR — its `runError` latch throws for the next event whatever it is, with no RUN_STARTED exemption — where TypeScript resumes on RUN_STARTED and reduces the second run normally. A cross-SDK divergence, recorded here rather than resolved: closing it means giving EventStreamConverter the same reset-on-RUN_STARTED the TypeScript verifier has. The second run therefore never happens on this lane, so `messages`, `messageCount`, `eventTypes` and `eventPaths` are all restated for what it does deliver: the first RUN_STARTED and the RUN_ERROR, and no messages at all.
dotnet.errorContains: The run has already errored with 'RUN_ERROR'
